pain.status: Paid keys held up: zero failed calls across the 2026-10-08 benchmark. The reports come from the keyless MCP tier that opencode, Hermes and oh-my-openagent ship by default, where throttling can arrive as HTTP 200 text, not a 429, so failover never fires.
pain.play: Return a real 429 with Retry-After from the keyless tier, publish the free-tier limits, add built-in retry to exa-py/exa-js, and send failover PRs to opencode and Hermes.

sources.quote: opencode's built-in `websearch` is Exa-backed and rate-limited.
keyless Exa free-tier throttle arrives as HTTP 200 text
keyless chain collapses to Exa-only and fails with 429 under parallel agents
It would be helpful to have a retry mechanism for each API call (e.g. search, fetch etc) - to handle 429 errors.

pain.status: List price is $7 per 1,000 searches (up to 10 results) plus $1 per 1,000 extra results; HN threads place that at the top of a $0.25-$7 range. Out-of-credit 402s surface mid-run inside agents. Responses already carry costDollars, which is a head start on transparency.
pain.play: Ship a usage-alert webhook and a soft-limit mode so agents see 'credits low' before a 402, add costDollars to every SDK type, and publish a cost-per-correct-answer comparison using the benchmark's precision lead.

sources.quote: Web search API pricing for AI agent usecases has always felt so expensive for what it is
Exa charges 7$ per 1000 queries, and charges additionally for each result that is out of top-10.
web_search_tool fails silently when Exa credits are exhausted
Request failed with status code 402. Please check your query and try again.

pain.theme: Empty results and filters (includeDomains / excludeDomains / dates)
pain.status: Exa had the best precision@5 (40%) and best insurance accuracy (75%) in the 2026-10-08 benchmark, but 12 of 90 responses came back empty. Developers report strict domain matching, ignored exclusions and junk redirect results.
pain.play: Return a 'why empty' hint (which filter removed results) and auto-relax filters on request; match subdomains in includeDomains; publish a filter cookbook.

sources.quote: The Exa API is returning empty result arrays for all queries, despite successful HTTP responses.
this is unlike google search operators, which capture the broad domain.
Domains in excludeDomains are still included in results
Search results include email-tracking redirect links (link.cfr.org) with empty title

pain.status: In the benchmark 44% of Exa results fell inside the requested date window and the newest relevant result had a median age of 8.2 h. Contents are cache-first unless maxAgeHours is set, and a failed live crawl falls back to cache without a clear signal.
pain.play: Add a crawl-failure reason and 'served stale' flag to statuses, document maxAgeHours units and defaults in every SDK, and send fixes to wrappers (Hermes, Agno) that drop freshness options.

sources.quote: The failed live crawl silently falls back to the cache.
Exa's Contents API is cache-first when maxAgeHours is omitted, and supports maxAgeHours=0 for an always-live crawl.
A null or empty optional number is coerced to 0, so maxAgeHours: null forces live crawling
web_search passes livecrawl_timeout=30 — Exa's unit is milliseconds, so live-crawl gets a 30 ms budget

pain.status: Client p50 was 1,106 ms and p95 3,997 ms in the benchmark: fast typical calls with a long tail. Reports describe hangs and MCP endpoint timeouts more than slow averages.
pain.play: Set default client timeouts in exa-py/exa-js, publish a status page with p95 for mcp.exa.ai, and contribute timeout handling to Agno, smolagents and gpt-researcher wrappers.

sources.quote: Exa search sometimes hangs indefinitely.
MCP call failed: TimeoutError: MCP call timed out after 300.0s (configured timeout: 300.0s)
Exa MCP endpoint (mcp.exa.ai) timing out while REST API works
stalled API requests can block MCP/extension execution.

pain.status: Sign-in to first API key took 95 s in 13 steps in the benchmark, the slowest of four. MCP users also hit sign-in errors, OAuth-vs-header doc conflicts, keys in URLs, and Cloudflare 403s from datacenter and Workers IPs.
pain.play: Cut key creation to a one-screen flow, return 401 to unauthenticated MCP calls so OAuth clients can sign in, make header auth the documented default, and allowlist major agent clouds (Cloudflare Workers).

sources.quote: Because the Exa MCP server does not respond with 401, but instead interprets unauthenticated requests as throttled free-tier requests, MCP Clients do not allow users with paid Exa accounts to authenticate.
The OAuth instruction misdirects Claude Code setup.
Passing it as a query parameter increases the risk that it gets logged by our production systems.
mcp.exa.ai and api.exa.ai both return Cloudflare 403 from datacenter IP

pain.theme: SDK changes, changelogs and docs drift
pain.status: exa-js (4.36M npm downloads/month) and exa-py (5.41M PyPI/month) are widely used, but users ask for changelogs, hit removed features after minor upgrades, and see raw JSON parse errors when an HTML error page comes back.
pain.play: Publish release notes per version with a breaking-change label, add typed errors for non-JSON responses, keep docs examples tested in CI, and upstream base_url support to Agno and CAMEL.

sources.quote: Today I updated from 2.8.0 to 2.10.2 and immediately noticed that the tweet category had been removed.
Right now I'm just looking at individual commits to get a clue what a new version number includes
'Exa' object has no attribute 'research' when using sample SDK code from Exa dashboard (v1.13.1)
seeing a mismatch between the docs and the live hosted MCP server

pain.theme: MCP server packaging and tool exposure
pain.status: exa-mcp-server had 159,677 npm downloads in the last month, about 1.8x tavily-mcp (86,778), and is in the official MCP Registry as ai.exa/exa. The friction is packaging churn: npx bin failures, tools missing after releases, oversized outputs and schema errors.
pain.play: Run a client test matrix (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, opencode, Open WebUI) on every release, cap tool output size by default, and keep the Claude Code plugin version in lockstep with the hosted tools.

sources.quote: now even when passing the --tools parameter, we only get web_search_exa and get_code-context_exa
NPX package broken on Linux - HTTP endpoint only exposes 2 tools instead of 7
returns 112k+ characters, cannot consume results in claude code
The official Claude Code plugin currently has several packaging inconsistencies
